sections.h2: How can I sell my house fast in Buffalo?
sections.html: Three paths exist: an agent listing, a for-sale-by-owner sale, or a direct purchase by a company like ours. The direct purchase moves fastest because no lender has to sign off on the buyer. Condition usually decides it. A worn two-family with deferred repairs, or a rental that failed the city's inspection, drags on a listing, while an investor can price the same house as it stands.

Renters outnumber owners in Buffalo. Only 43.0% of homes house the person who owns them, which means much of the stock is income property that must satisfy city registration rules before it can legally collect rent. The 2025 estimate is 274,613 residents, a 1.3% drop since April 2020, living in 119,630 households.

  • Median value of an owner's home: $164,200
  • Median gross rent: $1,046 a month
  • Median household income: $50,041

With values in that range, a repair bill can swallow a large share of a sale price, and a buyer will subtract it from any bid. An investor who plans to rent the house out works backward from the rent figure, so a unit that cannot yet pass inspection has to be priced lower to account for the work.

A house's address can move its value as much as its condition does, and buyers compare neighborhoods closely. The city's Green Code, adopted in 2017, replaced zoning rules more than sixty years old. If you plan a change of use, such as turning a house into a different number of units, ask City Hall which code district applies before you spend money.

sections.h2: Winter wear on a Buffalo house
sections.html: Lake-effect snow brings heavy winters, and roofs, gutters, porches and plumbing absorb the abuse, so inspectors look at those first. If a worn roof is beyond your budget, an investor will fold the replacement into the price instead of asking you to do it.

Rental rules in the city affect how easily a tenant-occupied house changes hands, so read them before you list.

  • Every non-owner-occupied one- or two-family house must be on the Rental Registry, whether or not it is occupied. Some three-family and mixed-use buildings are covered as well.
  • A new registration costs $100. Since January 1, 2025 the yearly fee has been $50 for a single unit and $100 for a two-unit house.
  • Registered properties are scheduled for proactive inspection and must hold a Certificate of Rental Compliance. A property that fails cannot operate as an income property, and the tenants cannot be evicted for unpaid rent.
  • Landlords certify that a house built before 1978 may contain lead hazards, and the city will refuse a Certificate of Occupancy where lead paint is a hazard.
  • The city's Lead Hazard Reduction Grant offers up to $12,000 per unit in the Upper West Side and Schiller Park neighborhoods.

The Rental Registration office is at 65 Niagara Square, Room 304, phone 716-851-5621.

Short-term rentals need a separate license. A stay under six months qualifies, every address needs its own license, and renewal is yearly. The license stays with the owner, so a new owner has to apply from the start. Non-owner-occupied properties also need a special use permit. The short-term rental team answers at 716-851-4077.

sections.h2: What a tenant means for your sale
sections.html: A sale can go ahead with tenants in place. Ask the Rental Registration office whether your address holds a current Certificate of Rental Compliance. A rental that fails inspection cannot operate as an income property, and a buyer will see that on the city's records. LLCs or corporations owning rentals must also supply owner details at renewal, so check that yours is up to date.

Buyers of rental houses in Buffalo look at paperwork before paint. A current Certificate of Rental Compliance tells them the house can collect rent today. A missing one means they must pay for repairs, schedule an inspection and wait, all before the first tenant pays. That delay is why failed-inspection houses linger on the market and why investors discount them.

If your house is older than 1978, the lead paint certification adds one more item. A cash buyer can take a house with lead issues and fold the cost into the offer. A buyer using a mortgage may find the lender balks. Knowing which route fits you before the first showing saves weeks, and it keeps you from accepting an offer that quietly depends on a lender.

When you speak to a buyer, offer the registry paperwork first, then the tax balance, then the deed. That order answers their three biggest questions in the sequence they usually ask them.

sections.h2: Erie County deed costs and transfer tax
sections.html:
Deeds for Buffalo houses are filed with the Erie County Clerk.

Erie County Clerk charges on a residential deed
ChargeAmount
Statutory recording fee$45, plus $5 for each written page
TP-584 transfer tax form$10 to file
RP-5217 transfer report (residential or farm property)$125 to file
Transfer tax, owed by the seller$4.50 per $500 of price ($2.00 state, $2.50 county)

The clerk keeps the original deed on record and mails it back after the indexing is verified. A Notice of Sale or Transfer of Ownership form accompanies a residential deed. The deed is signed and notarized, then filed together with the TP-584 and the RP-5217.

Inside the city, the Department of Assessment and Taxation reviews every deed filed to update ownership records. Its tax office sends delinquent notices, helps owners set up court-ordered payment plans and runs an annual In Rem foreclosure auction, so a house with unpaid city taxes is worth sorting out before an offer is signed. Ask that office for a current balance, including sewer rent, before you close, so no unpaid charge surprises you at the table.

1. Confirm whether the house is on the Rental Registry and whether its Certificate of Rental Compliance is current.
  2. Ask the tax office for a balance that includes sewer rent.
  3. Collect the deed and a mortgage payoff statement.
  4. Compare any cash offer with what a listing would net after repairs and the months you would carry the house.
  5. At closing, the deed, TP-584 and RP-5217 go to the Erie County Clerk with the fees above.

faqs.q: What if tenants still live in my Buffalo house?
faqs.a: A sale can go ahead with tenants in place. Ask the Rental Registration office whether your address holds a current Certificate of Rental Compliance, since a rental that fails inspection cannot operate as an income property.

faqs.q: What does registering a Buffalo rental cost?
faqs.a: The first application costs $100. After that the yearly fee is $50 for one unit or $100 for two units, and LLCs or corporations owning rentals must also supply owner details at renewal.

faqs.q: Which side owes New York transfer tax on a Buffalo closing?
faqs.a: The seller does. Erie County's clerk posts a combined rate of $4.50 for each $500 of price: $2.00 to the state and $2.50 to the county.

faqs.q: Is a permit required for nightly stays at a Buffalo house?
faqs.a: A Short-Term Rental License is required for any stay under six months. The license stays with the owner, so a purchaser who wants to continue short-term renting has to file a new application.

faqs.q: Which office files a Buffalo deed?
faqs.a: The Erie County Clerk's Office. The deed is signed and notarized, then filed together with Form TP-584 and the RP-5217 report, and the clerk returns the original by mail once it is recorded.
